printed_page_note: no printed page number is on this exposure. The `No.` of the printed heading runs into the binding at the top right of the leaf, where the page curves into the gutter and the facing leaf shows through, and no figure can be read there. Recorded as unknown, not inferred from the sorted filename order, which is not the book order.
division_note: the printed heading reads `by the Marshal of the ____ District (or Territory) of` with `Illinois` written in the blank in ink; the district blank is unfilled and no enumerator's name appears on the exposure. No division is recorded.
line_count_note: coverage.json inventoried this image at 28 lines `to the nearest line`, and T-0644 recorded that no uniform pitch fits the observed ink clusters - neither 28 lines at 84.6 px nor 31 at 76.5 px. Read line by line against a measured, sheared column map it carries 32. The inventory count is superseded by this reading. The grid was NOT fitted as a pitch: each line here is either anchored by cross-column coincidence (an entry in commerce, manufactures or the learned professions standing on the same y as the TOTAL group) or, where the industry columns are empty on that line, assigned on glyph grouping alone. Every record says which of the two it is in `row_anchor`, so a later reading can attack the weak ones without re-deriving the strong ones. 17 of the 32 lines are cross-column anchored.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL - number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
geometry_note: the leaf is skewed on the exposure, less than on 33S7-9YYJ-8D: the printed vertical rules drift about 6 px to the left over 2,000 px of y (-0.003 px per px of y). Every column band used in this reading is sheared by that slope before its ink is taken. The map, measured at y=750 and confirmed against the rules visible at magnification: body band y 578-2948; footer row between y 2948 and 3030; TOTAL x 1115-1306 with the digits standing in its right half; mining 1306-1376, agriculture 1376-1441, commerce 1441-1506, manufactures and trades 1506-1585, navigation of the ocean 1585-1668, navigation of canals lakes and rivers 1668-1744, learned professions and engineers 1744-1818. The seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns were measured on this image for the first time, from the printed headers read at magnification: universities or colleges 3167-3228, number of students 3228-3292, academies and grammar schools 3292-3355, no. of scholars 3355-3433, primary and common schools 3433-3497, no. of scholars 3497-3562, no. of scholars at public charge 3562-3620.
tool_note: tools/read_census_continuation.py still does not run on this image: it exits `no industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS`, as T-0644 recorded. It was not weakened to fit. The reading here was made the way 8D's was - at magnification against a measured, sheared column map - with connected-component geometry used only to locate ink and never to decide a digit.
alphabet_note: THE HAND'S DIGITS WERE CALIBRATED BEFORE THE TOTAL COLUMN WAS READ, against the three industry columns whose footer figures are known. Commerce, manufactures and the learned professions were read glyph by glyph and each closes EXACTLY on its printed footer (15, 12, 8). Two forms in this hand are what that calibration settled, and both had been misread on the first pass: (a) a `1` here often carries a heavy horizontal ENTRY-FLAG at its head, which detaches into its own connected component and reads at first sight as a 7 - commerce y1224 and manufactures y625 are both of this form and both must be 1, because their columns close at 15 and 12 only if they are; a true 7 in this hand, as in the footer's own 157, has a long tail that falls well below the writing line. (b) a `4` is an arm, a crossbar and a vertical - the manufactures cell on line 14 is the sheet's one fully inked example. The 4 this calibration reaches is the same 4 that 33S7-9YYJ-6H and 33S7-9YYJ-DD reach by other routes; the reading here did not start from theirs, which is why it is worth recording that it agrees with them.
right_edge_note: The form's last column - white persons over 20 years of age who cannot read and write - stands beyond x3620 where the leaf curves into the gutter and the facing page shows through. It cannot be seen on this exposure and is not recorded as empty in either direction: the sheet does not say so. The `no. of scholars at public charge` column immediately before it is visible and is blank on every line.
closure_note: The enumerator totalled his own columns at the foot of the sheet. Those figures are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and every committed column is checked against them in `column_closure`. A column that does not close keeps its residual, and its reading is NOT adjusted to make the total come out.

footer_as_read.learned_professions_glyph_note: the figure is a closed double loop and the sheet's own 5 - in the footer's 157 - carries a top bar this glyph does not have. Read 8, as T-0644 recorded it.
footer_as_read.schools_footer_note: the footer also repeats the schools figures: 1 under primary and common schools and 25 under the no. of scholars beside it. Both match the single body entry on line 1.
footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: the slaves, pensioners and deaf/dumb/blind/insane blocks carry no figure at the foot of this sheet, and no entry on any of its 32 lines.

closes_note: Every column on this sheet closes exactly EXCEPT the family totals, which read 155 against a printed 157 - a residual of -2 over 32 lines, and nothing was altered to close it. Commerce reads 15 against a printed 15; manufactures and trades 12 against 12; the learned professions 8 against 8; the schools pair 1 and 25 against a footer that repeats 1 and 25; mining, agriculture and both navigation columns are empty on every line and carry no footer figure. THE TWO-STROKE FIGURE IS WHAT THE RESIDUAL TURNS ON, and the arithmetic is the reason it is read as 4. Five lines - 2, 11, 13, 14 and 21 - carry two parallel strokes with their starts 28 to 32 px apart and no crossbar inked; line 1 carries three strokes, and its last two are only 14 px apart, which is half a digit pitch, so they are one digit and the line is 1 then that digit. Read those six figures as 4 and the column stands at 155 against 157. Read them as 11, which is how the different hand on 33S7-9YYJ-8D was read, and the column stands at 190 against 157 - a residual of +33 that no other reading on this sheet can absorb. The 4 reading is also what the sheet's own ink supports: the manufactures cell on line 14 is a fully inked arm-crossbar-vertical 4, and its two heavy strokes start 24 px apart, inside the range the TOTAL pairs occupy. This is a finding about THIS hand and is not carried back to 8D, which is a different hand on a sparser sheet. The residual of -2 is left where it falls; three lines (9, 22 and 30) carry a lone crescent read as 6 with the ascender not inked, and those are the readings a second pass should attack first. CORROBORATION, ARRIVED AT INDEPENDENTLY. This sheet's arithmetic was worked before its neighbours' were consulted, and it lands on the same key they do. 33S7-9YYJ-6H settles the same figure not by arithmetic but by the enumerator's own hand: its printed page footing is a 1 followed by that two-stroke figure twice, standing in the tens and units of a three-figure number where nothing but a single digit can stand, so he wrote 144 and in writing it showed the figure is a 4 (T-0645). 33S7-9YYJ-DD reaches it a third way, from a page whose family totals close exactly on their own footing. Three sheets, three independent routes, one answer. What this sheet adds is the closest the deposit has come to a closing TOTAL column: -2 over 32 lines, against 8D's +15 and 6H's -7.

pairing.why: T-0642's pairing test wanted two keys from this sheet and had neither: its TOTAL footing was unread and its line count stood at an inventory figure `to the nearest line`. Both are supplied here, and with them the sheet is ruled OUT of image group 1 rather than left open. It carries 32 entries and foots at 157; no left sheet in images 1-25 carries 32 entries - eleven of the twelve are ruled to 31 and the twelfth to 30 - and none foots at 157. The nearest populations, 160 on printed 231 and 152 on 33S7-9YYJ-9MX, are refused on both keys. So this sheet's left half is not in this image group at all, exactly as 33S7-9YYJ-8D's is not: the deposit is ordered by sorted filename and not by the book, so a left sheet and its own continuation are in the same group only by accident. That is a fact about the deposit, not a failure of the reading. Recorded in left_sheet_population_key.json as the test's second positive result.
pairing.page_population_key_note: the printed footer figure - the enumerator's own arithmetic over his own sheet - which is what a left sheet's age-band sums are matched against. The line-by-line reading of the same column is 155; that is a second reading and is NEVER the key. Both are published because the pairing test has to know they differ on this sheet, though by far less than on 8D, where they differ by 15.
